patients with lower viral loads and higher CD4 counts at the start of follow-up had lower viral loads at the end of follow-up.
the evolution of the VL in patients with HIV infection is influenced by a variety of individual factors.
the evolution of the VL in patients with HIV infection depends on their immunological and virovirological status at the beginning and end of their follow-up.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the factors which are associated with the evolution in the viral load of a group of patients with HIV infection.
the identification of factors that determine the evolution of VL and that may be of interest in the management of patients with HIV infection.
a study of the temporal evolution of the VL of patients with HIV infection, and with the identification of those variables which are most associated with the evolution.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the VL of patients with HIV infection is determined by the following factors: the immunological state at the onset, the basal VL, the gender of the patients, their adherence to the treatment and their clinical care.

the evolution of the VL in patients with HIV infection depends on the immunological and virogenic status at the onset of their follow-up, on the antiretrovirus treatment they have received and on the unit where they have been cared for.
the evolution of the VL depends on the initial immunological and virolological status of the patient, the type of antiretrovial treatment received and the duration of the follow-up.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the initial VL and the CD4 count determine the evolution of the VL.
patients who have a better virological and immunological status at baseline will have better evolution in the follow-up.
the initial VL and CD4+ cell count are the main factors that determine the evolution of the VL in the first years of follow-up.
The main takeaway from our work is that
patients with a low VL are more likely to have a low VL in the future.
the immunological and virogenic state at the beginning of the follow-up is the most relevant factor in the evolution of the VL.
